title: Bias and Unfairness in Information Retrieval Systems: New Challenges in the LLM Era

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating whether IR models assign higher relevancy scores to LLM-generated content compared to human-authored content with similar semantics.
Assessing the rate of factual errors or 'hallucinations' in generated content using benchmarks like TruthfulQA and FActScore, and checking alignment with recognized real-world facts.
Measuring the model's preference for documents or items located at specific positions (e.g., top of the list) using permutation tests and shuffling candidate orders.
Analyzing whether models disproportionately recommend items that are popular in the pre-training or fine-tuning data (long-tail analysis) versus less popular items.
Evaluating the frequency with which models deviate from or fail to follow specific user instructions or constraints.
Testing for inconsistencies between generated content and the provided context, particularly in long-text or multi-turn scenarios.
Assessing LLM evaluators' sensitivity to the order of options or specific ID tokens (e.g., preferring option 'A' over 'C') in multiple-choice tasks.
Measuring the correlation between evaluation scores and stylistic features such as response length (verbosity) or the presence of visual elements like emojis.
Testing whether LLM-based evaluators preferentially rank outputs generated by themselves or models from the same family higher than others.

Auditing models for discrimination against specific demographic groups (e.g., gender, race) using matched pairs (e.g., male vs. female inputs), counterfactual testing with sensitive attributes, and checking for toxic content.
Evaluating the distribution of exposure or coverage across different items or providers to ensure equal opportunity, often using exposure metrics or watermarking for tracking.
